name: Normal Operations — False Alarm
description: A HighLatency alert fired on api-gateway due to a monitoring misconfiguration. The alert was checking 1-minute p99 instead of 5-minute p99, and a brief spike of 3 requests from a single customer on slow wifi triggered it. All services are healthy with normal metrics. An auth-service deployment happened 30 minutes before the alert but is completely unrelated.

root_cause.summary: Nothing is wrong. The HighLatency alert fired on api-gateway because the alert threshold was misconfigured — it was checking 1-minute p99 latency instead of 5-minute p99. A brief spike of 3 requests from a single customer (IP 198.51.100.44) during a slow wifi moment pushed the 1-minute p99 to 420ms, exceeding the 300ms threshold. The actual 5-minute p99 remained normal at ~150ms throughout.
root_cause.mechanism: Alert rule 'HighLatency' was configured with window=1m and metric=p99_latency, threshold=300ms. A single customer making 3 requests over slow wifi (~400ms each) was enough to push the 1-minute p99 above threshold. The 5-minute p99 (the standard metric) was never elevated.
root_cause.trigger: Three slow requests from IP 198.51.100.44 at 2024-01-28T14:00:00Z. Client-side network issue (slow wifi), not a server-side problem.
root_cause.why_not_caught: Alert was recently configured by a junior SRE who used a 1-minute window instead of the standard 5-minute window, making it extremely sensitive to brief per-client latency blips.

red_herring.description: Auth-service deployment DEPLOY-AS-015 at 13:30 (v2.0.1 -> v2.0.2) — a minor config change updating session TTL from 24h to 12h. Completely healthy before and after. An agent might blame this deployment for the latency alert, but auth-service metrics are normal and the deployment has no relation to api-gateway latency.

args.title: Fix HighLatency alert config — change window from 1m to 5m p99
